Below is the complete 12‑week programme tailored for your 29‑year‑old recreational climber with right subacromial impingement (4 months into physio), cleared for pain‑free range only and no overhead loading. It includes the 3‑phase strength plan, hangboard/climbing prep, two cardio sessions/week, nutrition for body recomposition, daily/weekly mobility, and a Saturday finisher. Share this with her physio and adjust any exercises that provoke symptoms.

Quick reference
- Duration: 12 weeks (3 phases of 4 weeks).
- Frequency: Strength 3×/week (Mon/Wed/Fri), Cardio 2×/week (Tue + Sat or Tue + Thu depending on schedule), Saturday finisher once/week (30–45 min), daily mobility (10–12 min), deeper mobility 1–2×/week.
- Restrictions: No painful range; no overhead loading with right arm; avoid positions provoking impingement (end‑range abduction + external rotation). Always follow pain rules: stop sharp pain, numbness/tingling or persistent pain >24 h — consult physio.
- Progression: Conservative; increase load only after 2 pain‑free sessions at current load. Regress (less ROM, lighter load, more assistance) if symptoms appear.

Phase breakdown
Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4: Adaptation & motor control
- Goals: Pain‑free movement, scapular control, rotator cuff endurance, baseline horizontal push/pull strength.
- Intensity: RPE 5–7. Tempo controlled.
- Typical week:
  - Mon (Session A): Floor/neutral single‑arm press 3×8–10; chest‑supported single‑arm row 3×8–10; TRX rows 3×10–12; band ER 3×12–15; serratus work 3×10–12; farmer carries 2×60s.
  - Wed (Session B): Seated cable row 3×8–10; neutral lat pulldown 3×8–10; face pulls 3×12–15; prone Y/T/W 2–3×10; split squats 3×8–10; deadbug/Pallof 3×30–45s.
  - Fri (Session C): Low‑incline chest press 3×8–10; single‑arm cable row 3×8–10; TRX assisted pull‑up eccentrics 3×4–6; band IR 3×12; scapular isometrics 3×10s; kettlebell RDL 3×8–10.
- Cardio: Cardio1 steady 30–40 min zone 2 (Tue). Cardio2 interval/traverse easy (Sat) — foundational intervals.
- Hangboard/climb: None yet unless physio clears very basic traversing.
- Mobility: Daily 10–12 min routine, pre‑session warm‑ups.

Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8: Build strength & unilateral control; introduce light climbing prep
- Goals: Increase load, single‑arm strength, eccentric control, begin low‑dose hangboard and traversing if pain‑free and physio OK.
- Intensity: RPE 6–8, incorporate slower eccentrics (3–4 s).
- Typical week:
  - Mon (A — Strength push focus): Single‑arm DB horizontal press 4×6–8; chest‑supported single‑arm row 4×6–8; TRX/incline rows 3×8–10 (3s ecc); band ER + pull‑apart superset 3×10–12; hanging core 3×8–12.
  - Wed (B — Pull + posterior): One‑arm cable lat rows 4×6–8; deadlift 3×5 (moderate); face pulls 4×10–12; Y/T dumbbell raises 3×10; goblet/Bulgarian split squat 3×8.
  - Fri (C — Integrated): Chest‑supported incline press 4×6–8; heavy single‑arm row 4×6–8; eccentric pull‑ups 3×4–6; rotator cuff circuit 3 rounds; farmer carry 3×40–60s; plank 3×30–60s.
- Cardio: Cardio1 steady 40–55 min (Tue). Cardio2 intervals/climb specificity — e.g., treadwall/traverse sets (Sat).

Structure overview
- Duration: 12 weeks, broken into 3 × 4‑week phases (Adaptation, Build, Performance).

- Focus per session: each workout is upper‑body dominant but includes lower‑body and core to maintain whole‑body balance and climbing transfer.
- Restrictions: No overhead pressing or loaded overhead positions with the right arm. Avoid end‑range abduction/external rotation positions that provoke impingement. Use pain‑free range only; mild discomfort that settles is acceptable only if approved by physio.

- Emphasize scapular upward rotation control (serratus anterior), scapular retraction (lower/mid traps), posterior cuff strengthening (ER/IR at safe ranges), and thoracic extension mobility.

- Pulling focused on scapular control: supported rows, single‑arm chest‑supported rows, TRX horizontal rows, lat pulls without extreme shoulder abduction.
- Rotator cuff work: low‑load internal/external rotation in safe ranges with bands/dumbbells, eccentric focused work and isometrics as needed.

- Stop any movement that causes sharp pain, new numbness/tingling, or increasing pain afterward.

Below is the complete 12‑week programme tailored for your 29‑year‑old recreational climber with right subacromial impingement (4 months into physio), cleared for pain‑free range only and no overhead loading. It includes the 3‑phase strength plan, hangboard/climbing prep, two cardio sessions/week, nutrition for body recomposition, daily/weekly mobility, and a Saturday finisher. Share this with her physio and adjust any exercises that provoke symptoms.

Quick reference
- Duration: 12 weeks (3 phases of 4 weeks).
- Frequency: Strength 3×/week (Mon/Wed/Fri), Cardio 2×/week (Tue + Sat or Tue + Thu depending on schedule), Saturday finisher once/week (30–45 min), daily mobility (10–12 min), deeper mobility 1–2×/week.
- Restrictions: No painful range; no overhead loading with right arm; avoid positions provoking impingement (end‑range abduction + external rotation). Always follow pain rules: stop sharp pain, numbness/tingling or persistent pain >24 h — consult physio.
- Progression: Conservative; increase load only after 2 pain‑free sessions at current load. Regress (less ROM, lighter load, more assistance) if symptoms appear.

Phase breakdown
Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4: Adaptation & motor control
- Goals: Pain‑free movement, scapular control, rotator cuff endurance, baseline horizontal push/pull strength.
- Intensity: RPE 5–7. Tempo controlled.
- Typical week:
  - Mon (Session A): Floor/neutral single‑arm press 3×8–10; chest‑supported single‑arm row 3×8–10; TRX rows 3×10–12; band ER 3×12–15; serratus work 3×10–12; farmer carries 2×60s.
  - Wed (Session B): Seated cable row 3×8–10; neutral lat pulldown 3×8–10; face pulls 3×12–15; prone Y/T/W 2–3×10; split squats 3×8–10; deadbug/Pallof 3×30–45s.
  - Fri (Session C): Low‑incline chest press 3×8–10; single‑arm cable row 3×8–10; TRX assisted pull‑up eccentrics 3×4–6; band IR 3×12; scapular isometrics 3×10s; kettlebell RDL 3×8–10.
- Cardio: Cardio1 steady 30–40 min zone 2 (Tue). Cardio2 interval/traverse easy (Sat) — foundational intervals.
- Hangboard/climb: None yet unless physio clears very basic traversing.
- Mobility: Daily 10–12 min routine, pre‑session warm‑ups.

Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8: Build strength & unilateral control; introduce light climbing prep
- Goals: Increase load, single‑arm strength, eccentric control, begin low‑dose hangboard and traversing if pain‑free and physio OK.
- Intensity: RPE 6–8, incorporate slower eccentrics (3–4 s).
- Typical week:
  - Mon (A — Strength push focus): Single‑arm DB horizontal press 4×6–8; chest‑supported single‑arm row 4×6–8; TRX/incline rows 3×8–10 (3s ecc); band ER + pull‑apart superset 3×10–12; hanging core 3×8–12.
  - Wed (B — Pull + posterior): One‑arm cable lat rows 4×6–8; deadlift 3×5 (moderate); face pulls 4×10–12; Y/T dumbbell raises 3×10; goblet/Bulgarian split squat 3×8.
  - Fri (C — Integrated): Chest‑supported incline press 4×6–8; heavy single‑arm row 4×6–8; eccentric pull‑ups 3×4–6; rotator cuff circuit 3 rounds; farmer carry 3×40–60s; plank 3×30–60s.
- Cardio: Cardio1 steady 40–55 min (Tue). Cardio2 intervals/climb specificity — e.g., treadwall/traverse sets (Sat).
- Hangboard (Weeks 5–8 if cleared): 1×/week, large jugs/open‑hand repeaters: 6–8 reps 7s hang/3s rest × 2–3 sets; progress to 8–10 reps or 8–10s hangs as tolerated. Emphasize scapular engagement; assisted as needed.
- Traversing/climb: 1×/week technique & endurance: 3–4 sets of 4–6 min continuous traversing on big holds.
- Mobility: daily + 1 deeper session/week.

Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12: Performance, power and climb‑specific peak
- Goals: Peak horizontal push strength and single‑arm control for trip, increase climbing specificity, careful taper.
- Intensity: High intensity Weeks 9–11 (RPE 8–9), taper Week 12.
- Hangboard/climb: increased but conservative — repeaters 8s/4s × 3 sets in Weeks 9–10; possible strength hangs or mixed sessions in Weeks 11 if pain‑free and cleared; reduce or stop heavy hangs in Week 12 (taper).
- Cardio: Keep steady state and interval work but reduce intensity/volume close to heavy push days and during Week 12 taper.

  - Power: light med‑ball speed work 2×5.

- Session A (Push + Pull + Core)
  - Warm‑up (10 min): 5 min bike + scapular prehab (wall slides, serratus punches, band pull‑aparts) + rotator cuff activation.
  - Main: Single‑arm horizontal press (floor or low incline) 3–5 sets per week varying reps as phase progresses (8–10 → 6–8 → 4–6 → 3–5 → 2–4 in peak).

- Frequency: weekly; 30–45 min.

  - Option A (conditioning, moderate): 4 rounds 40s on/20s off — kettlebell swings, TRX rows, reverse lunges, med‑ball passes; grip finisher (farmer hold) + cooldown.

- Tuesday: Cardio 1 — steady state (30–60+ min, zone 2)
- Wednesday: Strength Session B (pull + lower)

- Reduce overall volume by ~40–50% and keep 1–2 maintenance intensity sets for neuromuscular readiness.
- Avoid heavy hangboard and reduce interval cardio. Keep climbing on‑wall work light and focused on technique and pacing.
- Maintain protein & carbs slightly higher 48 h pre‑climb; ensure sleep and travel logistics don’t disrupt recovery.
